q: What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. Multiples of 6: 6, 12. The smallest common one is 12.

q: What is 15% of 200?
The sum of the three angles of a triangle is:
e: The angle sum property of a triangle states the angles add up to 180°.

q: What is the area of a rectangle that is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
e: Area = length × width = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

q: Which of these numbers is prime?
e: 21 = 3×7, 27 = 3×9 and 33 = 3×11. 29 has no divisor other than 1 and itself.

q: (a + b)² is equal to:
e: Expanding (a + b)(a + b) gives a² + 2ab + b².

What is the value of sin 30°?
e: sin 30° = 1/2 is a standard trigonometric value.

q: What is the value of tan 45°?
e: In a 45°–45°–90° triangle the two legs are equal, so tan 45° = 1.

q: What is the 10th term of the AP 2, 5, 8, 11, …?
The discriminant of ax² + bx + c = 0 is:
e: Discriminant D = b² − 4ac. It decides the nature of the roots.

q: What is d/dx (sin x)?
e: The derivative of sin x with respect to x is cos x.

q: What is ∫ 2x dx?
e: The integral of 2x is x², plus the constant of integration C.

Which gas do plants take in from the air for photosynthesis?
e: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight to make food and release oxygen.

q: What is the SI unit of force?
e: Force is measured in newtons (N).

q: Which part of the cell is called its powerhouse?
e: Mitochondria release energy from food, which is why they are called the powerhouse.

q: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
e: The heart pumps blood through the blood vessels.

q: What is the pH of a neutral solution such as pure water?
e: pH 7 is neutral. Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.

q: Which acid is found in lemon?
e: Lemons and other citrus fruits contain citric acid.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
e: Electric current is measured in amperes (A).

q: Ohm's law states that:
e: Potential difference V is proportional to current I: V = IR.

q: Approximately what is the speed of light in vacuum?
e: Light travels at about 3 × 10⁸ metres per second in vacuum.

q: Which lens is used to correct myopia (short-sightedness)?
e: A concave (diverging) lens moves the image back onto the retina.

q: The loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called:
e: Transpiration is the evaporation of water through stomata in leaves.

q: What is the atomic number of carbon?
e: Carbon has 6 protons, so its atomic number is 6.

q: “To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction” is which law?
e: This is Newton's third law of motion.

q: What is the formula for kinetic energy?
e: A body of mass m moving at speed v has kinetic energy ½mv².

q: Choose the correct plural of “child”.
e: “Child” has an irregular plural: children.

q: Choose the antonym of “ancient”.
e: Ancient means very old; its opposite is modern.

q: Fill in the blank: She ___ to school every day.
e: A singular subject in the simple present takes “goes”.

q: What is the past tense of “write”?
e: The past tense of write is wrote; written is the past participle.

q: Choose the synonym of “happy”.
e: Joyful has nearly the same meaning as happy.

q: Change to passive voice: “The cat ate the fish.”
o: The fish was eaten by the cat.
The fish is eaten by the cat.
The cat was eaten by the fish.
e: Simple past active becomes “was/were + past participle” in the passive.

q: Which part of speech is the word “quickly” in “He ran quickly”?
e: “Quickly” tells how he ran, so it is an adverb.

q: Choose the correct sentence: “Neither of the boys ___ present.”
e: “Neither” takes a singular verb, so “was” is correct.

q: What is the capital of India?
e: New Delhi is the capital of India.

q: What is the capital of Bihar?
e: Patna is the capital city of Bihar.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
e: Jawaharlal Nehru became India's first Prime Minister in 1947.

q: Which river is the national river of India?
e: The Ganga was declared the national river of India in 2008.

q: Where did the Revolt of 1857 begin?
e: The revolt began with the sepoys at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

q: On which date did the Constitution of India come into effect?
e: It came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which of these Indian states?
e: Jharkhand is one of the eight states crossed by the Tropic of Cancer.

q: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
e: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757.

q: “सूर्य” का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
e: दिनकर, भास्कर और रवि सूर्य के पर्यायवाची हैं।

q: “अंधकार” का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
e: अंधकार का विलोम प्रकाश है।

q: “पवन” का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
e: पवन, वायु और हवा समानार्थी शब्द हैं।

q: “विद्यालय” का संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
e: विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय (दीर्घ संधि)।

q: “राम ने खाना खाया।” वाक्य में कर्ता कौन है?
e: क्रिया को करने वाला कर्ता होता है। यहाँ खाने का काम राम ने किया।

q: “पुस्तक” शब्द का लिंग क्या है?
e: पुस्तक स्त्रीलिंग शब्द है (एक पुस्तक, अच्छी पुस्तक)।
